chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) regarding the man who divorces his wife,
he said: 'He is more rightful with reverting back to her, for as long as the blood has not fallen regarding the third (menstruation)'.

key_terms.الدَّمِ الثَّالِثِ: The third blood/menstruation; referring to the third menstrual period which marks the transition to irrevocable divorce in this context.
key_terms.رَجْعَة: Right of reversion; the husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period after a revocable divorce.

ai.seo_question: When does a man lose the right to take his divorced wife back during the waiting period?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise temporal boundary for *rajʿah* (revocable divorce), linking it to the completion of the *Iddah* waiting period marked by the third menstrual cycle. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the husband retains unilateral authority to restore the marital bond without a new contract until this specific physiological marker confirms the finality of the divorce phase.
